spec.title: Answers per second by status
spec.description: What k6 got back, by HTTP status (status 0 = no answer within 15 s). Steady state is all 202. Look for 503 right after each kill and how long they last. Surprising: 503 or status 0 while only one broker is down with acks=all, or 202 while two are down with acks=all. k6 series are not marked stale after a run, so the last value can linger.

spec.title: Share of requests not accepted (%)
spec.description: Requests that did not get 202, as a percent of all requests, split by acks variant (the acks label exists after the first K4 run). The shape (a burst, a plateau, a decay) matters more than the number.

spec.title: Request latency p50 and p99 (k6)
spec.description: Latency seen by the client. Expect a spike in p99 when a leader disappears (the API waits for the new leader up to its 5 s send timeout) and fast 503s (low latency) when the health check has opened the breaker. Surprising: latency above 15 s (k6 timeout).

spec.title: Run phase (from run.sh)
spec.description: ep_k4_phase written by run.sh into the node_exporter textfile: 0 steady, 1 one broker down, 2 two brokers down, 3 both started again, -1 no run. Use it to line up every other panel with the kills.

spec.title: Brokers seen by the cluster
spec.description: kafka_brokers from the kafka-exporter (brokers listed in the cluster metadata, asked from the brokers that are still alive). Drops 3 -> 2 -> 1 at the kills and returns at the restart. Caveat: the exporter needs a live broker to answer and may show a gap while the quorum is lost.

spec.title: In-sync replicas per partition (topic k4-events)
spec.description: Size of the ISR of each of the 6 partitions. Starts at 3. With one broker down it should fall to 2 for the partitions that had a replica there; with two down to 1 (or stay stale if the quorum is lost and the ISR cannot be changed). min.insync.replicas is 2: below it acks=all writes are refused.

spec.title: Leader of each partition (topic k4-events)
spec.description: Broker id of the leader per partition (1, 2 or 3; -1 = no leader). A change of line = a leader election. Surprising: -1 for a long time while one broker is down (the other brokers should take over within seconds).

spec.title: Partitions below min ISR
spec.description: How many of the 6 partitions have fewer than 2 in-sync replicas: the partitions where acks=all cannot be written. Also the under-replicated count (ISR smaller than the replica list).

spec.title: API 503 and Kafka send errors per second
spec.description: ep_http_503_total by reason and ep_kafka_send_errors_total by type (server side). kafka_unavailable = the health check or breaker refused the request; overloaded = queue full. The send error types name what Kafka said (not enough replicas, timeout, ...). The 503 and send-error series appear only after the server has run.

spec.title: API health check and circuit breaker
spec.description: ep_kafka_health_ok (1 = last check passed: every partition has a leader and at least minIsr in-sync replicas, minIsr = 2 for acks=all and 1 for acks=1), ep_kafka_breaker_state (0 closed, 1 open, 2 half-open), ep_kafka_producer_connected. Expect health 0 and breaker open while acks=all is below min ISR. With acks=1 I expect the health check to stay 1 as long as every partition has a leader.

spec.title: Messages acknowledged vs failed by Kafka (server side)
spec.description: Rate of messages the producer got an ack for (ep_kafka_messages_acked_total) and of messages in batches that failed (ep_kafka_messages_failed_total). Compare with the k6 202 rate: the difference is what the API rejected before sending.

spec.title: Produce round-trip time per broker (p99)
spec.description: ep_kafka_broker_rtt_seconds p99 from the client statistics of librdkafka, per broker address. A broker that was killed stops answering (its series stops or freezes).

spec.title: Records written per partition (offset growth)
spec.description: Rate of the end offset of each partition of k4-events (kafka-exporter). Shows which partitions keep receiving records while a broker is down. Caveat: needs a leader to answer, so a partition without a leader shows a gap.

spec.title: Broker cores busy (host CPU, pinned brokers)
spec.description: Busy share of the cores the broker containers are pinned to (variable cpu_brokers). Expect the survivors to work harder when one is gone (more leaders each) and a burst when a broker restarts and catches up.

spec.title: API process CPU and event-loop delay
spec.description: CPU seconds per second used by the API process (1 = one full core; pinned to 2 cores) and the event-loop lag. A pile of waiting requests can cost CPU and lag.

spec.title: Producer queue and batcher queue
spec.description: Messages waiting in librdkafka's own queue and in the micro-batcher queue (ep_kafka_client_queue_messages, ep_batcher_queue_depth). They grow while Kafka does not accept writes and the API still takes requests (acks=1 with a dead leader, or before the breaker opens).

spec.title: k6 virtual users in use
spec.description: k6_vus against k6_vus_max. In-flight requests pile up as VUs when the API is slow to answer (10,000 would be 2000 req/s x 5 s). Hitting the max means k6 drops iterations.

spec.title: k6 dropped iterations (must be 0)
spec.description: dropped_iterations: arrivals k6 could not start because no VU was free. Any value above 0 in the steady part makes the run invalid. During two_down it can be non-zero if many requests wait; that is then part of the finding, not a generator fault.

spec.title: Generator CPU (k6 cores)
spec.description: Busy share of the cores k6 is pinned to (cpu_k6). Keep under about 70% so the generator is not the limit.

spec.title: Server cores and monitoring cores busy
spec.description: Busy share of the API cores (cpu_server) and of the monitoring cores (cpu_monitoring, Prometheus, Grafana, exporters, Postgres). A saturated API core would blur the result.

spec.title: Audit drain: rows inserted per second
spec.description: ep_consumer_rows_inserted_total of the consumer-sinks that run after each load to put the topic into Postgres for the audit. Nothing should be running here during the load. A run is audited when this returns to 0 after a hump.

2. The mechanism: leaders, ISR and the API's reaction
3. Resource view: where the cost lands

spec.description: CPU ids the server group is pinned to (0,6), as a regex for cpu=~"$cpu_server"

spec.name: cpu_brokers
spec.label: CPUs: brokers (pinned)
spec.description: CPU ids the brokers group is pinned to (1,7,2,8), as a regex for cpu=~"$cpu_brokers"

spec.name: cpu_k6
spec.label: CPUs: k6 (pinned)
spec.description: CPU ids the k6 group is pinned to (3,9,4,10), as a regex for cpu=~"$cpu_k6"
